description: An open-source, self-hostable application platform for building and operating applications on Kubernetes

summary.one_liner: Cloudness is an open-source, self-hostable platform for deploying and managing applications, servers, and databases on Kubernetes clusters you own.
summary.what_it_does: Cloudness provides a Heroku-style deployment platform that runs on your own Kubernetes cluster, which the README says can be cloud, on-premises, or Raspberry Pi hardware. It manages applications, environments, and databases, with pre-configured templates for PostgreSQL, Redis, MySQL, and Valkey. The README describes built-in CI/CD pipeline support for automated builds and deployments, real-time log streaming, and multi-tenant organizations and projects with authentication and authauthorization. Configurations are stored as Kubernetes manifests, so resources keep running if you stop using Cloudness. The backend is written in Go with the Gin framework, and the frontend uses Templ, Alpine.js, and Tailwind CSS.
use_cases: deploy apps to my own Kubernetes cluster
run apps on Raspberry Pi Kubernetes
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash (installation script; the URL is missing from the README)
git clone (repository URL missing from the README)
notable: Stores all app, database, and service configuration as Kubernetes manifests, avoiding vendor lock-in
Works with any Kubernetes cluster, including cloud, on-premises, and Raspberry Pi
Local development runs without Docker, since it is a plain Go binary
Pub/Sub can use Redis or an in-memory provider
caveats: Requires an existing Kubernetes cluster; the README says you only need one, but setup is not described in detail
Several roadmap items (multi-cloud, canary/blue-green deployments, GitOps, marketplace) are unchecked and not yet available
Installation and configuration details are deferred to external documentation not included in the README
